## Overview {.tabset}

The **`r herb`** herbarium was compared against the
[Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/),
the official checklist of Brazilian plants and fungi, to identify taxonomic gaps
— accepted species recorded in FFB but not yet represented in the collection.

```{r kpi-boxes}
htmltools::tags$div(
  class = "kpi-row",
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-green",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_ffb_total)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "FFB accepted species")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-blue",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_in_herb)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label",
                        paste0("Species in ", herb,
                               " (", d$pct_present, "%)"))
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-red",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_missing)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label",
                        paste0("Missing taxa (", d$pct_missing, "%)"))
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-amber",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_endemic_missing)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Missing Brazilian endemics")
  ),
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "kpi-box kpi-gray",
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-value",
                        scales::comma(d$n_genera_absent_all)),
    htmltools::tags$div(class = "kpi-label", "Genera entirely absent")
  )
)
```

---

## Gaps by Major Taxonomic Group

The chart below shows how the taxonomic gaps are distributed across the major
taxonomic groups recognized by FFB. The Flora e Funga do Brasil
covers vascular plants, bryophytes, algae, and fungi. Understanding which
groups contribute most to the gap highlights broad collection priorities.

```{r plot-group, fig.height=4}
ggplotly(d$plots$group, tooltip = "text") %>%
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15))
```

---

## Top Missing Families

The following table ranks the **`r nrow(d$family_gap)`** families with missing
species from most to least critical. Only the top 30 are displayed. Families at
the top of the chart represent the greatest opportunity for targeted collecting
expeditions.

```{r table-family}
top30_fam <- head(d$family_gap, 30)
DT::datatable(
  top30_fam,
  colnames = c("Family", "Missing species"),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 1. Top 30 families with the most missing species."
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 15,
    dom = "ftp",
    order = list(list(1, "desc"))
  )
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle("n_missing",
                  background = DT::styleColorBar(top30_fam$n_missing, "#ffd6da"),
                  backgroundSize = "98% 88%",
                  backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
                  backgroundPosition = "center")
```

---

## Top Missing Genera

The bar chart below shows the 20 genera with the highest number of missing
species. Bars coloured in **red** indicate genera that are **entirely absent**
from `r herb` — not a single species of that genus is represented in the
collection. Bars in **green** indicate genera that are only partially
represented.

```{r plot-genus, fig.height=6.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$genus, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r table-genus-absent}
if (nrow(d$genera_absent_all) > 0) {
  DT::datatable(
    head(d$genera_absent_all, 50),
    colnames = c("Genus", "Family", "Missing species", "In herbarium"),
    rownames = FALSE,
    caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
      style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
      paste0("Table 2. Top 50 genera entirely absent from ", herb,
             " (", scales::comma(nrow(d$genera_absent_all)),
             " genera total).")
    ),
    options = list(
      pageLength = 20,
      dom = "Bftp",
      buttons = c("copy", "csv")
    ),
    extensions = "Buttons"
  ) %>%
    DT::formatStyle(
      "in_herb",
      backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(FALSE, "#ffd6da")
    )
}
```

---

## Geographic Distribution of Gaps

### Map of missing taxa by Brazilian state

The choropleth map shows the number of missing taxa per Brazilian state. Darker
states have more species absent from `r herb` that occur there according to FFB.
Hover over a state to see the count.

```{r leaflet-map, fig.height=5}
tryCatch({
  states_sf <- geobr::read_state(year = 2020, showProgress = FALSE)
  states_sf  <- dplyr::left_join(states_sf, d$state_gap, by = "abbrev_state")
  states_sf$n_missing[is.na(states_sf$n_missing)] <- 0

  pal <- leaflet::colorNumeric(
  palette = c(
    "#F2D7C9",
    "#E6B8A2",
    "#D98E73",
    "#CD5C5C",
    "#BC4749",
    "#A4243B",
    "#8A1538",
    "#6D071A"
  ),
  domain = states_sf$n_missing,
  na.color = "#f5f5f5"
)

  leaflet::leaflet(states_sf) %>%
    leaflet::addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>%
    leaflet::addPolygons(
      fillColor = ~pal(n_missing),
      fillOpacity = 0.75,
      color = "white",
      weight = 1.2,
      label = ~paste0(name_state, ": ", scales::comma(n_missing),
                      " missing taxa"),
      labelOptions = leaflet::labelOptions(
        style = list("font-size" = "12px"),
        sticky = FALSE
      ),
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<b>", name_state, "</b><br>",
        "Missing taxa: <b>", scales::comma(n_missing), "</b>"
      )
    ) %>%
    leaflet::addLegend(
      pal = pal,
      values = ~n_missing,
      title = "Missing taxa",
      position = "bottomright"
    )
}, error = function(e) {
  htmltools::p("Map could not be rendered: ", e$message,
               style = "color: #6c757d; font-style: italic;")
})
```

### Missing taxa by state (bar chart)

```{r plot-state-bar, fig.height=5.5}
state_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  d$state_gap,
  ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(abbrev_state, n_missing),
               y = n_missing,
               fill = n_missing,
               text = paste0(abbrev_state, ": ", scales::comma(n_missing)))
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F2D7C9", high = "#A4243B",
                               guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of missing taxa",
                title = paste0("Missing taxa by state — ", herb)) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", color = "#A4243B"),
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

ggplotly(state_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

---

## Phytogeographic Domains

The bar chart summarises how missing taxa are distributed across Brazil's
six major phytogeographic domains (biomes). Taxa may be counted in more than
one domain if they occur across multiple regions.

```{r plot-domain, fig.height=4.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$domain, tooltip = "text")
```

---

## Endemism of Missing Taxa

The chart below breaks down the `r scales::comma(d$n_missing)` missing taxa
into **Brazilian endemics** (species whose entire range lies within Brazil) and
**non-endemic** species. Endemics are of particular conservation concern when
absent from the herbarium.

```{r plot-endemism, fig.height=3.5}
ggplotly(d$plots$endemism, tooltip = "text")
```

---

## Complete List of Missing Species

The table below shows all `r scales::comma(d$n_missing)` species missing from
`r herb`. Use the search box to filter by any column.

```{r table-missing, echo=FALSE}
display_cols <- c("group", "family", "genus", "taxonName",
                  "scientificNameAuthorship")
display_cols <- display_cols[display_cols %in% names(d$taxon_not_in_herb)]

DT::datatable(
  d$taxon_not_in_herb[, display_cols, drop = FALSE],
  colnames = c("Group", "Family", "Genus",
                 "Taxon name", "Authorship")[seq_along(display_cols)],
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  extensions = "Buttons",
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    paste0("Table 3. All ", scales::comma(d$n_missing),
           " taxa absent from ", herb, ".")
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 20,
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"),
    scrollX = TRUE
  )
)
```
